summary: No new trust boundary. The only untrusted-ish input is observed opponent stats; they still go through the unchanged observedBySeat validation (RangeError) before scaledWidthPct, and resizeRange is a pure, bounded pass over the 169-entry bundled HAND_ORDER, so there is no resource-exhaustion path. Even a NaN width would end with a finite set (the narrowing branch adds the default's classes and stops). hand-order.json is a bundled build-time asset with format and version unchanged, validated at import. Its seeded computeEquity is used only to rank hands offline and plays no part in fairness (dealing). No new dependencies, no secrets, no file, shell or network operations. The package.json change only adds a test file to test:slow.
